name: 0apt
iocPatterns: Automatic shadow copy deletion via vssadmin or internal commands
Usage of Brute Ratel/Cobalt Strike for lateral traffic
Execution of PowerShell and WMI for discovery
keyCapabilities: Supply chain compromise of third-party providers
recommendedActions: Monitor and block network connections to known Tor exit nodes and its identified IP range.
Implement blocks on the use of unauthorized remote access tools like NetBird or OpenSSH.
Audit and restrict usage of WMI and PsExec across internal segments to prevent lateral movement.
Deploy EDR rules to detect and alert on any calls to shadow copy deletion commands (e.g., vssadmin).*
Scan for and block known Rust-compiled binaries in production environments that are not part of the baseline.
Implement robust data exfiltration alerts at the perimeter, focusing on high volumes of outbound traffic to unusual IPs.
Secure and audit configuration files—particularly those related to databases/credentials—against hardcoded secrets.
Conduct targeted awareness training regarding "ClickFix" scripts and other phishing-based delivery methods.
campaignsText: Since its debut in early 2026, 0APT has displayed an aggressive operational tempo meant to establish a presence in the RaaS ecosystem. They specialize in 'double extortion' campaigns where evidence of data breach is publicized on a dedicated leak site via Tor to maximize pressure on victim organizations. The group’s rapid claim cycle and high volume of reported victims suggest they may leverage automated tools or prior-obtained credentials to inflate their perceived success, while still maintaining technical rigor in their core encryption technologies.
description: 0APT is an emerging Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) actor that utilizes a custom Rust-based encryptor to conduct double-extortion attacks against high-value targets in the infrastructure, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors. While the group employs several 'hoax' tactics—such as inflating victim counts via fake data—their underlying technical infrastructure, including Tor-based C2 and automated shadow copy deletion, presents a tangible threat to enterprise security.
goals: 0APT's primary objective is financial gain through a double-extortion ransomware model. Their targeting profile is broad and aggressive, spanning critical infrastructure, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, energy, and government entities globally. By focusing on high-stakes industries in the United States, Europe, and Asia, they seek to maximize leverage during negotiations using stolen data that could cause severe reputational or regulatory damage if leaked.
